question: What incentive values does the SuSI Program's ADI offer for net metered non-residential projects located on rooftops, carports, canopies, and floating solar in New Jersey?
gold_answers: The ADI Program offers $110 per SREC-II for net metered non-residential projects smaller than 1 MW and $100 per SREC-II for projects between 1 MW and 5 MW. Public entities can receive an additional $20 adder, making it $130 per SREC-II for smaller projects and $120 per SREC-II for larger ones.

question: What happens if a community solar garden does not comply with the regulatory policy's requirements?
gold_answers: If a community solar garden that has begun commercial operation is not in compliance with certain regulations, it must notify the commissioner and comply within 12 months. Failure to do so leads to revocation of its participation in the program.
prediction: the commissioner must revoke the solar garden's participation in the program

selected.title: 216B.1641 COMMUNITY SOLAR GARDEN.
selected.text: (e) The commission may approve, disapprove, or modify a community solar garden program.

selected.title: policy 22436
selected.text: A community solar garden that has begun commercial operation must notify the commissioner in writing within 30 days if the community solar garden is not in compliance with subdivision 6, 7, 9 or 10, and must comply within 12 months or the commissioner must revoke the solar garden's participation in the program.

selected.title: policy 22436
selected.text: (a) A utility must exclude from the fuel adjustment charged to a utility customer the net cost of community solar garden generation under this section if the utility customer (1) receives or is eligible for bill payment assistance, and (2) does not subscribe to a community solar garden under this section.

selected.title: 216B.1641 COMMUNITY SOLAR GARDEN.
selected.text: (f) Notwithstanding any other law, neither the manager of nor the subscribers to a community solar garden facility shall be considered a utility solely as a result of their participation in the community solar garden facility.

selected.title: policy 22436
selected.text: Community solar garden compensation.

selected.title: policy 22436
selected.text: The report must contain, at a minimum: (1) the energy produced by the community solar garden; (2) financial statements, including a balance sheet, income statement, and a sources and uses of funds statement; and (3) a list of the individuals that currently own and manage the subscriber organization.

selected.title: policy 22436
selected.text: (b) When allocating capacity to eligible community solar gardens, the commissioner must evaluate and prioritize capacity allocation to community solar garden applicants based on information provided in the community solar garden application regarding: (1) the degree to which subscribers, utility ratepayers, or the community surrounding the project receive the financial benefit of tax benefits and other incentives resulting from the community solar garden; (2) the scale of financial benefits the community solar garden delivers to LMI subscribers, affordable housing residents, and public interest subscribers, as well as the number of, and project capacity attributable to, LMI subscribers, affordable housing residents, and public interest subscribers; (3) community solar garden project ownership and financing arrangements that deliver benefits to public, nonprofit, cooperative, and Tribal entities; (4) whether the community solar garden uses nongreenfield locations, especially rooftops, carports, or sites that contain a hazardous substance, pollutant, or contaminant; (5) whether the community solar garden provides workforce development and apprenticeship opportunities, especially for workers who are Black, Indigenous, or Persons of Color; and (6) the resiliency benefits the community solar garden provides to the electrical grid or the local community.

selected.title: 216B.1641 COMMUNITY SOLAR GARDEN.
selected.text: Any plan approved by the commission must: (1) reasonably allow for the creation, financing, and accessibility of community solar gardens; (2) establish uniform standards, fees, and processes for the interconnection of community solar garden facilities that allow the utility to recover reasonable interconnection costs for each community solar garden; (3) not apply different requirements to utility and nonutility community solar garden facilities; (4) be consistent with the public interest; (5) identify the information that must be provided to potential subscribers to ensure fair disclosure of future costs and benefits of subscriptions; (6) include a program implementation schedule; (7) identify all proposed rules, fees, and charges; and (8) identify the means by which the program will be promoted.

selected.title: 216B.1641 COMMUNITY SOLAR GARDEN.

question: What does the City of Sacramento require for newly constructed buildings in terms of all-electric building requirements?
gold_answers:
All newly constructed buildings that are three stories or less shall be all-electric buildings if permit applications are filed on or after January 1, 2023.
**Context** - For building permit applications filed on or after January 1, 2023, except as provided in subsections 101.12.6 and 101.12.7, all newly constructed buildings that are three stories or less shall be all-electric buildings.

### QA Pair 2
**Question** - When does the requirement for all newly constructed buildings to be all-electric become mandatory in Sacramento?
**Answer** - The requirement becomes mandatory for buildings with permit applications filed on or after January 1, 2023.
**Context** - For building permit applications filed on or after January 1, 2023, except as provided in subsections 101.12.6 and 101.12.7, all newly constructed buildings that are three stories or less shall be all-electric buildings.

### QA Pair 3
**Question** - What exemptions are available for constructing mixed fuel buildings under the City of Sacramento's policy?
**Answer** - Limited exemptions include ground floor food service establishments for areas with cooking equipment, manufacturing or industrial facilities with process loads, and water-heating systems in regulated affordable housing where virtual net energy metering is unavailable.
**Context** - Limited exemptions for building permit applications filed on or before December 31, 2025, include ground floor food service establishments, manufacturing or industrial facilities, and regulated affordable housing.

### QA Pair 4
**Question** - When does the exemption for limited sectors end in relation to the all-electric building requirements in Sacramento?
**Answer** - The exemptions for limited sectors such as ground floor food service establishments, manufacturing or industrial facilities, and regulated affordable housing end on January 1, 2026.
**Context** - The section 101.12.1 and section 101.12.2 requirements to construct all-electric buildings shall not apply to sectors with limited exemptions until January 1, 2026

gold_answers: If you are income eligible and buying/leasing a new all electric vehicle, you can get an extra $1,000 rebate, bringing your savings to a maximum of $3,200.
